title: Global Climate Accountability Treaty
description: Binding emissions targets with financial penalties for non-compliance

preamble.text: Recalling the Paris Agreement and the urgent need for accelerated climate action
Deeply concerned by the widening gap between current emissions trajectories and the 1.5°C target
Recognizing the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities

operativeClauses.text: Establishes legally binding national emissions reduction targets aligned with limiting warming to 1.5°C
Creates an independent International Climate Compliance Body with authority to assess national performance
Institutes financial penalties for nations exceeding allocated carbon budgets, with revenues directed to adaptation funds
Mandates annual climate finance transfers of at least $200 billion to developing nations for adaptation and mitigation

title: International AI Governance Framework
description: Establishing a UN body to regulate frontier AI development

preamble.text: Noting the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence systems with potential for both benefit and harm
Concerned by the concentration of AI development capabilities in a small number of states and corporations
Recalling the Secretary-General's New Agenda for Peace and its technology governance provisions

operativeClauses.text: Establishes the International AI Governance Agency (IAGA) as a specialized agency under the UN system
Requires all states to submit frontier AI systems exceeding defined capability thresholds for mandatory safety assessments
Authorizes the IAGA to impose development moratoriums on AI capabilities deemed to pose existential risk
Creates a global AI benefit-sharing mechanism to ensure developing nations access transformative AI capabilities

title: Universal Nuclear Disarmament Resolution
description: Complete elimination of nuclear weapons with verification regime

preamble.text: Reaffirming the obligation under Article VI of the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons
Alarmed by the modernization of nuclear arsenals and the erosion of arms control frameworks
Welcoming the entry into force of the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons

operativeClauses.text: Demands the complete elimination of all nuclear weapons and their delivery systems within fifteen years
Establishes a universal verification regime with mandatory inspections of all nuclear-capable facilities
Requires all states possessing fissile material to declare stockpiles and submit to international controls
Provides legally binding security guarantees to states that have disarmed or foregone nuclear acquisition

title: Security Council Expansion and Veto Reform
description: Adding 6 permanent members with modified veto rights

preamble.text: Recognizing that the current composition of the Security Council does not reflect contemporary geopolitical realities
Noting that Africa, Latin America, and the majority of Asia have no permanent representation
Concerned by the paralysis caused by unilateral veto use on matters of peace and security

operativeClauses.text: Expands the Security Council to 21 members with 6 new permanent seats distributed as: 2 Africa, 2 Asia-Pacific, 1 Latin America, 1 Western European & Others
Modifies the veto mechanism to require two concurrent vetoes to block a resolution, preventing unilateral obstruction
Requires P5 members to provide written justification for any veto exercised, subject to General Assembly review
Establishes a 10-year review mechanism to reassess Council composition based on evolving global dynamics

title: Binding Cyber Warfare Norms
description: Prohibiting state-sponsored cyberattacks on civilian infrastructure

preamble.text: Deeply concerned by the increasing frequency of state-sponsored cyberattacks targeting civilian infrastructure
Noting that existing international humanitarian law applies in cyberspace but lacks specific enforcement mechanisms
Recalling the UN Group of Governmental Experts reports on responsible state behavior in cyberspace

operativeClauses.text: Prohibits all state-sponsored cyberattacks on civilian critical infrastructure including hospitals, power grids, water systems, and financial networks
Establishes an International Cyber Attribution Center with authority to attribute attacks through forensic investigation
Authorizes proportional collective response measures against states found responsible for attacks on civilian infrastructure
Creates a capacity-building fund to assist developing nations in protecting critical infrastructure from cyber threats

title: Universal Right to Clean Water
description: Declaring clean water access a binding human right with enforcement

preamble.text: Recalling General Assembly resolution 64/292 recognizing access to clean water as a human right
Alarmed that 2.2 billion people still lack access to safely managed drinking water
Noting the disproportionate impact of water scarcity on women, children, and marginalized communities

operativeClauses.text: Declares access to clean water and adequate sanitation a legally binding human right enforceable under international law
Requires all member states to submit national water access plans with measurable targets for achieving universal access by 2035
Establishes a Global Water Access Fund of $50 billion annually, financed through assessed contributions scaled by GDP
Prohibits the privatization of essential water services where it would restrict access for vulnerable populations

title: Digital Sovereignty and Data Governance
description: Establishing national rights over citizen data and digital infrastructure

preamble.text: Concerned by the extraterritorial reach of technology corporations in processing and storing citizen data
Recognizing that digital infrastructure constitutes critical national infrastructure

operativeClauses.text: Affirms that all nations have sovereign rights over the data generated by their citizens and within their territories
Requires technology corporations to establish local data processing centers upon reaching defined user thresholds
Establishes international minimum standards for data protection applicable to all cross-border data transfers
Creates a dispute resolution mechanism for conflicts between national data sovereignty and corporate data practices

title: Pandemic Prevention and Response Treaty
description: Binding obligations for pathogen sharing, vaccine equity, and early warning

preamble.text: Recalling the devastating global impact of the COVID-19 pandemic and the inequitable distribution of vaccines
Noting the failure of voluntary mechanisms to ensure timely access to medical countermeasures for developing nations

operativeClauses.text: Establishes legally binding obligations for pathogen sample sharing through the WHO within 24 hours of detection
Requires pharmaceutical companies receiving public funding to provide vaccine doses to developing nations at cost
Creates a standing pandemic response fund of $30 billion with automatic disbursement triggers
Mandates technology transfer for vaccine manufacturing to ensure regional production capacity on every continent

title: Outer Space Arms Control and Governance
description: Prohibiting weapons in space and establishing resource-sharing frameworks

preamble.text: Reaffirming the Outer Space Treaty principle that space shall be used exclusively for peaceful purposes
Alarmed by anti-satellite weapons tests and the militarization of orbital space

operativeClauses.text: Prohibits the placement, testing, or use of any weapons system in outer space or on celestial bodies
Bans anti-satellite weapons tests that generate orbital debris threatening shared space infrastructure
Establishes a Space Resource Governance Authority to manage equitable access to lunar and asteroid resources
Requires all space-faring nations to contribute to a Space Debris Mitigation Fund proportional to their orbital assets

title: Binding Treaty on Business and Human Rights
description: Mandatory corporate due diligence for human rights and environmental harms

preamble.text: Noting that the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights remain voluntary and inadequately implemented
Concerned by documented cases of corporate complicity in environmental destruction and labor exploitation

operativeClauses.text: Requires all transnational corporations to conduct mandatory human rights due diligence across their supply chains
Establishes an international tribunal with jurisdiction over corporate human rights violations exceeding national enforcement capacity
Creates a victims' compensation fund financed by penalties levied against non-compliant corporations
Grants affected communities legal standing to bring claims directly against corporations in international fora

title: Legal Framework for Climate Displaced Persons
description: Establishing legal status and rights for people displaced by climate change

preamble.text: Alarmed by projections that climate change may displace up to 1.2 billion people by 2050
Noting that the 1951 Refugee Convention does not cover persons displaced by environmental factors

operativeClauses.text: Establishes the legal category of 'climate displaced person' with defined rights under international law
Requires nations to accept climate displaced persons under a burden-sharing formula weighted by historical emissions
Creates a Climate Displacement Fund financed by major historical emitters to support relocation and adaptation
Prohibits the forced return of climate displaced persons to territories rendered uninhabitable by environmental change

title: Sovereign Debt Restructuring Mechanism
description: Creating a binding framework for developing nation debt relief

preamble.text: Concerned that 60% of low-income countries are in or at high risk of debt distress
Noting that current voluntary debt restructuring mechanisms are inadequate and inequitable

operativeClauses.text: Establishes an International Sovereign Debt Authority with binding arbitration powers over creditor-debtor disputes
Institutes automatic debt service suspension for nations experiencing GDP contraction exceeding 5% or declared humanitarian emergencies
Requires all creditors including private bondholders to participate in restructuring agreements reached through the Authority
Links debt repayment schedules to debtor nations' capacity to meet Sustainable Development Goals
